findings.statement: CA9 is first in the convergence ranking and has a moderate Open Targets ccRCC association [gene=CA9; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3088]. It is tractable by antibody, PROTAC and small molecule, and its drug history includes girentuximab (late clinical stage) and a radio-iodinated girentuximab imaging agent. UniProt places it at the cell and microvillus membrane, so it is accessible to antibodies and imaging. No ccRCC cell line depends on it in DepMap [gene=CA9; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0], it is not common essential, and it is not recurrently mutated [gene=CA9; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; padj=0.9578]. Its best case is as a surface biomarker and antibody or radioligand target, not as a cell-intrinsic dependency.

CD70 is fourth in the convergence ranking but has a weak Open Targets prior association [gene=CD70; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.0572]. Antibody tractability is at the advanced-clinical level, with cusatuzumab, vorsetuzumab, vorsetuzumab mafodotin and MDX-1411 in early clinical phases. UniProt describes it as a plasma-membrane ligand of CD27. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency [gene=CD70; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0], which fits an antigen target for conjugates or cell therapy rather than a driver.

EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) is the established ccRCC drug target, with belzutifan approved. Its Open Targets association is strong [gene=EPAS1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4871]. It is the only reviewed candidate with a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3], affecting a minority of ccRCC lines [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0.208], and it is not common essential. It is not recurrently mutated, as expected since HIF-2 alpha is activated by VHL loss.

MTOR is an established ccRCC drug target with many inhibitors (for example ridaforolimus, gedatolisib, sapanisertib) and a strong Open Targets association [gene=MTOR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.525]. It is recurrently mutated [gene=MTOR; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.0724]. Every ccRCC line depends on it [gene=MTOR; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=1], but DepMap flags it as common essential, which means a toxicity risk and a narrow therapeutic window rather than tumour selectivity.

KDR (VEGFR2) is an established target with approved drugs including axitinib, cabozantinib, tivozanib, cediranib and pazopanib, and a strong Open Targets association [gene=KDR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4566]. DepMap shows no ccRCC cell-line dependency [gene=KDR; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0], consistent with an anti-angiogenic, tumour-extrinsic mechanism that cell-line CRISPR screens cannot capture.

VHL has the top Open Targets ccRCC association [gene=VHL; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6466] and is the most frequent driver [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.4834]. Its loss of function stabilises HIF-alpha, the mechanistic basis of the HIF-2 alpha and VEGF axes. As a tumour suppressor it cannot be drugged by inhibition.

PBRM1 is the second recurrent driver [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362], with a strong Open Targets association [gene=PBRM1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6348]. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency [gene=PBRM1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0], as expected for a tumour suppressor. It is a stratification marker rather than a direct target.

SCARB1 has an Open Targets association driven mainly by genetic evidence [gene=SCARB1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.519], no listed drugs and predicted tractability only. UniProt places this HDL receptor at the cell membrane and caveolae, so it is antibody-accessible. DepMap shows no dependency [gene=SCARB1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0], so the target case is weak despite the surface location.

NNMT is tractable as a small-molecule target (druggable family with high-quality ligands) but has no clinical drug. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency [gene=NNMT; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0], so druggability without dependency makes a weak target case; it is better prioritised as a biomarker.

COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) is second in the convergence ranking but has a low Open Targets association [gene=COXFA4L2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.066], so its rank rests on omics and literature. The listed drugs (ME-344, metformin) act on mitochondrial complexes with uncertain target specificity, and it is untested as a ccRCC target.

PIGR is down in tumour and has an Open Targets association driven by genetic evidence [gene=PIGR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.7338] rather than drugs (none listed). It is an association-only, tumour-down biomarker candidate, not a target by inhibition.

ALDOB is strongly down in tumour with a prognostic association, but its Open Targets association is low [gene=ALDOB; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.0701] and no drugs are listed. It is a proximal-tubule loss marker for biomarker use only.

caveats: Open Targets association scores for CD70, COXFA4L2, NNMT and ALDOB are low; their ranking rests on omics, TCGA replication and literature rather than prior genetic evidence.

DepMap shows no selective ccRCC dependency for CA9, CD70, SCARB1 and NNMT, so these are antigen or biomarker cases, not driver targets. KDR efficacy is anti-angiogenic and invisible to cell-line CRISPR screens.
MTOR is common essential in DepMap, so its ccRCC dependency is not tumour-selective in absolute terms.
Drug stages are reported as returned by Open Targets; some listed drugs (metformin, ethoxzolamide) are not ccRCC-directed.
STRING interactions were not queried; tool-call budget focused on dependency and driver checks.
